chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
A man freed a share of his that was in a slave boy who had a debt on him. He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a partial share of a slave who has a debt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling of *kafāʾah* (manumission of a share) by stating 'No,' indicating that freeing only a portion of a slave who owes a debt does not automatically validate the emancipation or extinguish the debt proportionally without further agreement. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that partial manumission of a debtor-slave requires careful handling of the remaining financial obligation to ensure the slave's full freedom is achievable. The concise response highlights the precision of the Imams in distinguishing between partial ownership rights and the legal status of the slave's debt.
